**Finding: compliant (preferred position met).**

No MFN obligation runs against Bluefly anywhere in the Agreement:

- **§ 4.1 (Charges)** merely points to Service Option Attachments and Order Forms; no best-price or comparison undertaking.
- **§ 13.1** deals only with IBM's own right to change prices after twelve months — a Vendor right, not a Customer MFN.
- **§ 13.3 (Amendments)** requires a writing signed by both parties, so no unilateral price/terms-matching mechanic can be imposed.
- **§ 14.16 (Freedom of Action)** expressly confirms "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others," which is inconsistent with any obligation to extend IBM the best terms given to third parties.
- Targeted searches for most-favoured/most-favored, favorable terms, best price, third-party offers, right to match, benchmarking and comparable-customer language returned no hits.

Accordingly the single preferred element is already met and no redline was proposed. Note only for the record: the playbook's welcome case (an MFN *in our favour*) is likewise absent, so if better-pricing protection is commercially desired it would need to be negotiated in as a new term rather than as a redline under this rule.
